### F1. Rental start day: tier 2 fires more often than the rule allows
- Where: vsc_ext_claim_rental_reimbursement, factor rental_window_start, binding start_day (l.1062).
- Rule: "Rental days are counted from a start day: where the loaner went out after the day of the repair order's diagnosis, the day the loaner went out; where the loaner went out on that day and a line of the claim was denied after it, the day of that denial; otherwise the day of the repair order's diagnosis." Tier 2 ladder text: "the loaner went out on the day of the diagnosis and a line of the claim was denied after that day".
- Compute: `start_day: loaner_out if (loaner_out and diag_day and loaner_out > diag_day) else (denial_day if (denial_day and diag_day and denial_day > diag_day) else diag_day)`. Tier 2 never checks that the loaner went out on the diagnosis day, so it also fires when the loaner went out before the diagnosis.
- Witness: Exclusionary contract; loaner out 2025-06-02; diagnosis 2025-06-03; claim line denied 2025-06-05; loaner back and last labor 2025-06-09; charged 45.00/day. Compute starts 06-05: 5 days, 225.00. Rule starts on the diagnosis day 06-03: 7 days, 315.00. A loaner issued at check-in, the day before diagnosis, is an ordinary state.

### F2. "Later paid" fee tier counts any paid repair line on the claim number (kept and traded refunds)
- Where: vsc_ext_kept_vehicle_refund factor cancel_fee_standing (denied_claim l.1326, redecided_count l.1327, cancel_fee l.1329); vsc_ext_traded_vehicle_refund factor trade_fee_rule (l.2149, l.2150, l.2152).
- Rule (both): "...where the contract's latest denied claim line (by decision date; on a same-day tie, the one that appears first in the claim history) was later paid as a component-repair line on the same claim number, no fee is taken".
- Compute: `denied_claim: LATEST('vsc_ledger','claim_number', ..., event_type='vsc_claim_denied')` takes any line type; `redecided_count: COUNT('vsc_ledger', event_type='vsc_claim_paid', claim_line_type='component_repair', claim_number=denied_claim)`. Nothing ties the paid line to the denied line or requires it to come later.
- Witness (traded): Kessler Shield Powertrain has no rental benefit, so base vsc_evt_claim_benefits denies a rental request as component_not_covered. Claim CL-1: engine line paid 2025-06-01, rental line denied the same day. Compute: redecided_count 1, fee 0.00, refund 800.00. Rule: the denied rental line was never "later paid as a component-repair line", so a fee applies (725.00 with the coverage fee, or 775.00 with the trade loyalty fee). The same claim shape trips the kept-vehicle fee tier inside its free-look window.

### F3. The "already paid this way" check uses the claim number only (waiting, maintenance and coverage re-decisions)
- Where (each gates result): vsc_ext_waiting_denial_reimbursement already_repaid (l.777); vsc_ext_maintenance_denial_reimbursement already_repaid (l.1558); vsc_ext_coverage_denial_reimbursement already_repaid (l.1845).
- Rule (coverage; the others worded the same way): "the contract repays the holder once, as one paid component-repair line under the same claim number, repair order and component group at the repair order's odometer, and a denied line already repaid this way is not repaid again". Waiting: "...a denied line already paid this way is not paid again".
- Compute: `COUNT('vsc_ledger', event_type='vsc_claim_paid', claim_line_type='component_repair', claim_number=denied_claim)` — no repair-order or component-group filter, so a paid line for a different group under the same claim blocks the payment.
- Witness (coverage): Powertrain Plus, claim CL-4 on RO4; steering line paid by the contract; cooling line wrongly denied component_not_covered; line B carries customer-pay diagnosis 150.00 and labor 390.00 closed after the denial. Compute: already_repaid 1, result 0.00. Rule: cooling line in scope, repaid 390.00 + 150.00 − 100 deductible = 440.00. The charter declares exactly this per-group claim-line grain (distinguish_by claim_number, claim_line_type, component_group).

### F4. "The Kessler Care plan sold on the contract's purchase deal" also picks up standalone plans
- Where (all `CFIELD('maintenance','maintenance_plan_id', purchase_deal_id=F('purchase_deal_id'))`): maintenance plan_id (l.1563) gating visit_proof (l.1567); kept plan_id (l.1308), reading tier; traded plan_id (l.2128), measure-day tier; traded reading_plan (l.2132), reading tier.
- Rule wording: maintenance "the latest visit redeemed on the Kessler Care plan sold on the contract's purchase deal has not been reinstated and is dated on or before..."; kept "...the latest visit redeemed on the Kessler Care plan sold on the contract's purchase deal, where it has not been reinstated, records an odometer above the certified one..."; traded "where the Kessler Care plan sold on the contract's purchase deal carries a refund calculated on a cancellation for the vehicle being sold or traded...".
- Defect: a standalone contract has an empty purchase-deal id ("deal sold on (empty if standalone)"), and so does a standalone Kessler Care plan ("deal sold with (empty if standalone)"). The exact-match lookup returns the customer's first standalone plan, even one on another vehicle, where the rule says no such plan exists. Standalone contracts are within all three policies' scope (their waiting-period and credited-days clauses name them).
- Witness (maintenance): standalone Powertrain contract on VH1, engine line denied for lack of maintenance; the customer has standalone plan M9 on VH-OTHER with a visit 2025-04-01. Compute: plan_id M9, visit_proof 1, result 530.00. Rule: no plan sold on this contract's deal, line out of scope, result 0.00.

### F5. In-service-date terms: the starting-odometer tiers contradict the rule's own "miles before the sale date count as used" (kept and traded)
- Where: kept run_from (l.1316, factor term_miles_start); traded run_from (l.2141, factor trade_miles_start).
- Rule (identical in both): "the term miles run from a starting odometer: where the contract was sold on a purchase deal delivered after the contract's sale date with a delivery odometer above the odometer at sale, that delivery odometer; where it was sold on a purchase deal delivered to the holder's address on or before the sale date, the odometer at sale plus the deal's one-way delivery distance; otherwise the term start odometer."
- Same rule's assembly sentence: "...the unused mileage share is the starting odometer plus the term miles less the reading over the term miles, a share below zero counts as zero, and for a term counted from the in-service date the time and miles before the sale date count as used".
- Defect: a Kessler Shield Exclusionary Wrap contract counts its term from the vehicle's in-service date (term start odometer 0). If sold on a deal delivered late, or delivered to the holder's address, tiers 1 and 2 move the mileage start to the delivery odometer or to the sale odometer plus the delivery distance, counting pre-sale miles as unused, which the same sentence forbids. Two readings; compute takes one.
- Possible fix: exclude in-service-date terms from tiers 1 and 2, or scope the in-service clause.
